case_title: SOMESH CHAURASIA v. STATE OF M.P. & ANR.
previous_criminal_record: Yes, two prior convictions for murder
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.34; Arms Act s.25 (1) (1B)(a)
aggravating_circumstances: Prior convictions, political influence, obstruction of justice
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.302 IPC and awarded life imprisonment
neutral_facts: The accused, who had prior convictions for murder, was on bail following a suspended sentence for a previous conviction. An FIR was registered against him alleging involvement in the murder of the appellant's father. The police failed to properly investigate the FIR, leading to a closure report absolving the accused. Despite a warrant of arrest, the accused evaded capture. The High Court's order to delay investigation was found to obstruct justice, leading to the accused's eventual arrest. The case highlights issues of judicial independence and the administration of criminal justice.
